caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

raw_responses.Bulgarian:
The bar chart compares the perplexity of two pruning configurations, Per-Output and Per-Layer, at different sparsity rates. The x-axis represents the sparsity rate, labeled with values ranging from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%, while the y-axis represents perplexity on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^1 to 10^3. The chart features two series of bars, colored blue for Per-Output and orange for Per-Layer, allowing for a direct comparison between the two configurations. At lower sparsity rates (up to 50%), both configurations exhibit similar perplexity values below 10^1; however, as the sparsity rate increases, the perplexity values diverge, with Per-Output showing higher perplexity than Per-Layer at 60% and 70% sparsity rates. Notably, at 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output having slightly higher perplexity. The bars are grouped by sparsity rate, enabling a clear comparison between the two configurations at each rate.
